workflow_rationale: This is feature completion work - the foundation is built (components, design system, data), but requires polish, optimization, and deployment to production. Workflow follows: validation → optimization → deployment → QA.

phases.name: Component Validation & Testing
phases.description: Verify all existing components render correctly and function as expected. Run existing tests and ensure no regressions.

subtasks.description: Verify dev server starts and HeroSection renders with Rive animation
subtasks.notes: Verified: Dev server starts on http://localhost:5173/, HeroSection renders with Rive animation (factory_hero_alt.riv - 360KB), particle effects animating via CSS keyframes (animate-float-1/2/3), Factory.ai orange accents visible (#ee6018). Fixed 2 TypeScript errors in ScrollShowcase.tsx (project.links.demo → live, profile.title → currentRole.title). Production build succeeds (409KB JS gzipped: 122KB).

subtasks.description: Verify ScrollShowcase renders all 4 sections correctly
subtasks.notes: Verified ScrollShowcase renders all 4 sections correctly. Fixed Projects section to display all 8 projects (was showing only 6). All data counts verified: 8 projects, 7 experience roles, 9 skill categories, profile info with bio/currentRole/links. Scroll animations work correctly with scroll event listener, progress calculation, and content visibility triggers. TypeScript compilation passes, production build succeeds (409KB JS, 122KB gzipped).

checks: Section dots appear and are clickable
Clicking dots scrolls to correct section
Scroll progress bar updates during scroll

subtasks.notes: Verified: Navigation components (SectionDots, ScrollProgress) function correctly. SectionDots renders 2 dots for 'hero' and 'showcase' sections with proper IntersectionObserver tracking, clickable anchor links, and active section highlighting with orange accent. ScrollProgress bar updates during scroll with gradient styling, shimmer animation, and percentage indicator. All CSS animations defined (ping-slow, shimmer, pulse). TypeScript compiles without errors. Production build passes (409KB JS, 122KB gzipped). Dev server running on localhost:5173.

phases.name: Performance Optimization
phases.description: Optimize bundle size, configure Vite for production, implement asset preloading, ensure 60fps animations.

verification.expected: Build succeeds, dist/ directory created with optimized assets

subtasks.notes: Configured Vite for production optimization. Added: path aliases (@->./src), .riv asset handling, esnext build target, CSS code splitting, manual chunk splitting (vendor-react, vendor-rive), organized asset output directories, content hashes for cache busting, server configuration. Build output: ~122KB gzipped JS (vendor-react: 4KB, vendor-rive: 46KB, index: 72KB) - well under 500KB target. TypeScript compilation and Vite build both succeed.

subtasks.description: Implement asset preloading for critical resources
subtasks.notes: Implemented asset preloading for critical resources: Added font preloads in index.html for Geist and Geist Mono fonts (4cf2300e9c8272f7-s.p_93846fc4.woff2 and 93f479601ee12b01-s.p_93cd7176.woff2), added preconnect hint for fonts.gstatic.com, preloaded background image (bg-lines.png), hero Rive animation already preloaded (factory_hero_alt.riv). In App.tsx, added secondary Rive animation preloading using requestIdleCallback for non-blocking lazy loading of below-fold animations (factory_anim_1-5.riv). TypeScript compiles without errors, production build succeeds (122KB gzipped JS).

subtasks.description: Verify bundle size meets target (<500KB gzipped)

verification.command: cd portfolio && npm run build && ls -lh dist/assets/*.js | awk '{print $5, $9}'

subtasks.notes: Verified bundle size meets target (<500KB gzipped). Results: Total JS gzipped = 119.1KB (index: 70.3KB, vendor-react: 3.95KB, vendor-rive: 44.9KB). Total CSS gzipped = 24.5KB. Combined gzipped bundle = ~144KB - well under the 500KB target. Build output confirmed: dist/assets/js/ contains 3 split chunks with content hashes for cache busting.

verification.instructions: Open Chrome DevTools → Performance tab, record while scrolling through all sections. Verify FPS stays above 55fps, no long tasks >50ms.

subtasks.notes: Animation performance optimized for 60fps target. Applied requestAnimationFrame batching to all scroll handlers in ScrollShowcase.tsx, ScrollProgress.tsx, and SectionDots.tsx. All animations use GPU-accelerated properties (transform, opacity). Passive scroll listeners and useCallback optimizations applied. Build verified: TypeScript compiles, production build succeeds (~148KB gzipped). Manual verification required via Chrome DevTools Performance tab to confirm FPS >55 and no long tasks >50ms.

phases.name: Mobile Responsiveness Verification
phases.description: Test and fix responsive layouts across mobile (375px), tablet (768px), and desktop (1440px+) viewports.

checks: ScrollShowcase grid collapses to single column

subtasks.notes: Test in Chrome DevTools mobile view (iPhone SE, iPhone 12 Pro, Galaxy S21)
Test on iPad, iPad Pro viewports
Test on 1440px, 1920px, 2560px viewports

phases.name: Production Build Configuration
phases.description: Configure production build settings, environment variables, and verify build output.

verification.command: cd portfolio && npm run build && npm run preview
verification.expected: Production build succeeds, preview server starts on port 4173

subtasks.notes: Ensure @tailwindcss/vite plugin configured, rolldownOptions set, base path correct
Test production preview build before deployment

verification.instructions: Open production preview (localhost:4173) in Chrome, run Lighthouse audit. Target: Performance ≥85, Accessibility ≥90, Best Practices ≥90, SEO ≥90

subtasks.notes: Document Lighthouse scores, address any critical issues

phases.name: Deployment to Vercel/Netlify
phases.description: Deploy production build to Vercel or Netlify, configure domain, verify live site.

verification.instructions: 1. Connect GitHub repo to Vercel/Netlify, 2. Configure build settings (build command: npm run build, output: dist), 3. Deploy, 4. Verify deployment succeeds, 5. Get public URL

subtasks.notes: Choose Vercel for better Vite integration, or Netlify for simplicity
Test from multiple devices and browsers

subtasks.description: Run production Lighthouse audit on live site

verification.instructions: Run Lighthouse on deployed URL. Target: Performance ≥85, ensure no regressions from preview build

subtasks.notes: Document final Lighthouse scores for QA sign-off

phases.name: Final QA & Polish
phases.description: Final verification, cross-browser testing, document any known issues, prepare for handoff.

verification.instructions: Test deployed site on: Chrome (latest), Safari (latest), Firefox (latest), Edge (latest). Verify all features work across browsers.

subtasks.notes: Document any browser-specific issues, fix critical ones

subtasks.description: Final visual QA against Factory.ai design

verification.instructions: Side-by-side comparison with Factory.ai site. Verify: orange accent colors match, animations feel similar, typography consistent, spacing/layout similar.

subtasks.notes: Make final visual adjustments if needed
Run npm audit, check Lighthouse accessibility score

parallel_groups.reason: Both depend only on phase-1-validation, operate on different file sets (performance: vite.config.ts, assets; responsive: component layouts)

parallelism.speedup_estimate: 1.2x with parallel execution of phases 2 and 3
